wu: Flashcard Relay: Students line up in two teams. Teacher shows a G-M flashcard (e.g., 'goat'). First student runs, says the sound /g/, and tags the next. Team with all students fastest wins.
wuAlt: Phonics Bingo: Teacher calls out a sound (e.g., /m/), students cover the matching letter on their bingo card.
Sound Jump: Students jump when they hear the sound of their letter (G-M) called out.
pres: Teacher uses a story about 'Magic E' who changes short vowels to long vowels. Shows flashcards for 'tap' vs 'tape', 'kit' vs 'kite'. Models: 'This is tap. This is tape. Magic E makes the vowel say its name.' Students repeat.
presAlt: Realia Show: Teacher shows a real cap and a cape, contrasting /æ/ vs /eɪ/ sounds. Models: 'Cap. Cape.'
Video Clip: Short cartoon showing Magic E changing words like 'mad' to 'made'.
prac: CVCe Matching Game: Students work in pairs. Each pair gets a set of CVCe word cards (cake, bike, home) and picture cards. They match words to pictures and say them aloud. Teacher monitors and helps with pronunciation.
pracAlt: Whiteboard Relay: Teams take turns writing CVCe words from dictation (e.g., 'write home').
Phonics Hopscotch: Draw hopscotch with G-M letters. Students hop and say the sound of the letter they land on.
ls: Listen and Circle: Teacher plays a recording with pairs of words (e.g., 'tap/tape', 'kit/kite'). Students circle the word they hear on their worksheet. Checks if they can distinguish long vs short vowels.
re: Phonics Tag: Teacher calls out a sound (e.g., /b/). Students with 'b' cards run around. When teacher calls 'Magic E!', they freeze and say the long vowel sound (e.g., /baɪ/).
prod: Mini-Survey: Students ask 3 friends, 'What is your favorite CVCe word?' Friends answer, 'My favorite is __.' Students report back to the class, e.g., 'Fatima likes home.'
rw: Trace and Write: Students trace CVCe words (cake, bike, home) on a worksheet, then copy them 3 times each. Teacher checks for correct letter formation and magic e placement.
st: Story: Read 'The Magic E Adventure' book, pointing to CVCe words. End with 'Goodbye Song' (e.g., 'Bye Bye, Goodbye') and students line up for a high-five as they get a sticker.
g: Students jump when they hear the sound of their letter (G-M) called out.
Students flip over word/picture cards and match CVCe words to pictures.
Students roll a die, move, and say a CVCe word for the space they land on.
Teacher says, 'I spy with my little eye something with /eɪ/.' Students guess 'cake' or 'cape'.
Students hop on G-M letters and say the sound, then add 'Magic E' and say the long vowel sound.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a sentence with a CVCe word, e.g., 'I see a bike.'
Support: Use word/pairing cards with pictures to help match CVCe words.
hw: Play the matching game in the phonics library folder with a family member. Show them 3 CVCe words.
Draw a picture of your favorite CVCe word (e.g., home) and write the word underneath.
Ask your family: 'What is your favorite CVCe word?' and write it down.
tip: Use hand gestures for Magic E (e.g., a magic wand) to make the concept visual and memorable. Connect to local culture by using CVCe words related to Moroccan life, like 'home' or 'bike'.
